reason: A slow collision with the young world seems a useful way to follow its growth and surface.
expectation: The smaller body may merge with the world, adding material and possibly heating or marking its surface.

alternatives.reason: Fast stones may shatter a smaller body, but I want to follow the world first.

effect: The smaller body merged with the tracked world, adding mass and heat; I can now follow it into a larger impact.
reaction: The outcome matched my expectation, though the added heat makes the next collision interesting.
reason: A large impactor should advance the goal of following the world's interior and surface.
expectation: The impact will likely heat and disrupt the world, though I don't know how much material will remain.

effect: The larger impact melted much of the tracked world, so I can now follow its molten interior.
reaction: The substantial melting makes the impact's consequences clear.
reason: Metal-rich fragments seem relevant to what happens inside the molten world.
expectation: The fragments may join the world, with their metal possibly sinking into its interior.

alternatives.reason: This may start the shattered-body path, but I want to continue following the world first.

effect: The metal-rich fragments joined the world, and dense metal settled into a core; I can now follow its surface.
reaction: The separation of metal and rock was satisfying and matched my expectation.
reason: Fast stones may batter the tracked world's surface, advancing its goal.
expectation: The impacts will probably leave craters or other surface damage, though their exact effect is uncertain.

effect: The world now has a cratered solid surface over its dense interior, completing that goal; the shattered-body goal remains.
reaction: The craters matched my expectation and neatly completed the world's path.
reason: This is the only available combination and should start the remaining shattered-body path.
expectation: Fast stones may break one of the smaller rocky bodies into fragments that can gather again.

effect: A smaller body shattered, leaving fragments for the remaining gathering goal.
reaction: The contrast with the cratered larger world makes sense.
reason: This is the only available combination and may show the fragments gathering again.
expectation: The fragments may join the slowly approaching body, though the resulting object is uncertain.

effect: The fragments and incoming body formed a loose gravitationally bound world, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The rubble-world outcome was a satisfying contrast to the larger world's craters.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the molten world into a dense core made the separation of metal and rock concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial slow merger was straightforward and predictable, though it set up the later impacts.

surprise.text: The contrast between fast stones cratering the larger world and shattering a smaller body clarified how outcomes depend on the target.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the final gathering was the only offered action, but its purpose was clear.

continue.text: Yes. The contrasting collision outcomes and rubble-world ending make me curious about what happens to these bodies next.
